mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.75% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by >3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 3% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases financing costs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA by >10% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, which signals weak labor market quality and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE also rises over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for three consecutive months signals a shift toward consumption financing, which increases vulnerability to rate hikes and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA by >5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently below its 12-month moving average by more than 5%.
